Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 80, verses 1–16:

Tafsir of Surat 'Abasa

It is Makki.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

Many of the exegetes have mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was one day addressing some of the great men of Quraysh, and he was eager for their Islam. While he was speaking with them and conversing privately, Ibn Umm Maktum came up, and he had been among those who embraced Islam early. He began asking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about something and insisting upon it. The Prophet (ﷺ) wished that he would pause for that moment so that he could address that man, out of eagerness and desire for his guidance. He frowned in the face of Ibn Umm Maktum and turned away from him, and turned toward the other. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him. As for one who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention. Yet it is not upon you that he should not purify himself. And as for one who came to you striving, while fearing [Allah], from him you are distracted.﴾ That is: he may attain purification and cleansing within himself. ﴿Or be reminded and the reminder benefit him﴾ That is: he may attain admonition and restraint from the prohibitions. ﴿As for one who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention﴾ That is: as for the wealthy, you approach him, hoping he will be guided. ﴿Yet it is not upon you that he should not purify himself﴾ That is: you are not held accountable for him if he does not attain purification. ﴿And as for one who came to you striving, while fearing [Allah], from him you are distracted﴾ That is: you occupy yourself away from him. From here, Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) not to single out anyone for warning, but to treat equally in it the noble and the weak, the poor and the rich, the masters and the slaves, the men and the women, the young and the old. Then Allah guides whom He wills to the straight path, and His is the perfect wisdom and the decisive proof.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Muhammad (that is, Ibn Mahdi) narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah [from Anas] [[Note: What is between the brackets is not in the original text of Musnad Abi Ya'la nor in the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq. Is it from the copyists? I think it is an interpolation. And Allah knows best.]] concerning His words: ﴿He frowned and turned away﴾, Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was speaking with Ubayy ibn Khalaf, so he turned away from him, and Allah revealed: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him.﴾ Afterward the Prophet (ﷺ) would honor him.

Qatadah said: Anas ibn Malik informed me, saying: "I saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyyah wearing armor and carrying a black banner" – meaning Ibn Umm Maktum. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/431), and Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/282).]]

Abu Ya'la and Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from what he presented to him, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah who said: "﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum the blind man. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and kept saying: 'Guide me.' She said: While with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were some of the great polytheists. She said: The Prophet (ﷺ) kept turning away from him and turning toward the other, saying: 'Do you see any harm in what I say?' He would say: 'No.' Concerning this was revealed: ﴿He frowned and turned away.﴾" [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (8/261), and Tafsir al-Tabari (30/32).]]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated this hadith from Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi with its chain, similarly, then said: Some of them have narrated it from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: "﴿He frowned and turned away﴾ was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum," and he did not mention 'A'ishah in it. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3328).]]

I say: It is likewise in the Muwatta'. [[Muwatta' (1/203).]]

Then Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated, through the route of al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him.﴾ He said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was conversing privately with 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib – and he would often strive to reach them and eagerly desire that they believe – a blind man came toward him, called 'Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, walking while he (the Prophet) was conversing with them. 'Abdullah kept asking the Prophet (ﷺ) to recite a verse of the Qur'an to him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me from what Allah has taught you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him, frowned in his face, turned away, disliked his speech, and turned toward the others. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his private conversation and began returning to his family, Allah held back some of his sight, then he nodded his head, and Allah revealed: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded and the reminder would benefit him.﴾ When what was revealed about him was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) honored him, spoke to him, and said to him: "What is your need? Do you want anything?" And whenever he left his presence, he would say: "Do you have any need for something?" This was when Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿As for one who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you give attention. And it is not upon you that he should not purify himself.﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/32). Its strangeness is noted by what al-Suhayli transmitted in al-Rawd al-Unuf from his teacher Ibn al-'Arabi, who said: "The statement of the exegetes that the one who occupied the Prophet (ﷺ) was al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and al-'Abbas is entirely false, for Umayyah and al-Walid were in Makkah, while Ibn Umm Maktum was in Madinah and did not attend with them, nor did they attend with him; and they both died as disbelievers, one before the Hijrah and the other at Badr. Umayyah never intended Madinah, nor did he attend in its presence alone or with anyone else." End of quote.]]

There is in it strangeness and oddity, and its chain has been criticized.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab who said: Salim ibn 'Abdullah said, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Bilal calls the adhan at night, so eat and drink until you hear the adhan of Ibn Umm Maktum." He is the blind man concerning whom Allah revealed: ﴿He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him﴾, and he used to call the adhan together with Bilal. Salim said: He was a man blind in sight, so he would not call the adhan until people said to him – when they looked at the break of dawn – "Call the adhan." [[The original hadith is in Sahih Muslim (1092).]]

Likewise 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and many of the early and later scholars mentioned that it was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum. The well-known view is that his name was 'Abdullah, and it is said 'Amr. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder﴾ That is: this surah, or the admonition to equality among people in conveying knowledge, whether they be noble or lowly.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿Nay, indeed it is a reminder﴾ means the Qur'an. ﴿So whoever wills, let him remember it﴾ That is: whoever wills, let him remember Allah in all his affairs. It is possible that the pronoun refers to the revelation, as the context indicates it.

* *

His words: ﴿In honored scrolls, exalted, purified﴾ That is: this surah or the admonition, and both are interrelated; indeed, the entire Qur'an is ﴿in honored scrolls﴾, that is, esteemed and revered, ﴿exalted﴾, that is, of high rank, ﴿purified﴾, that is, free from defilement, addition, and deficiency.

* *

His words: ﴿By the hands of scribes﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: They are the angels. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). Qatadah said: They are the reciters. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-safarah" in Nabataean means the reciters.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the safarah are the angels, and safarah means intermediaries between Allah and His creation. From this comes the word safir: one who strives between people for reconciliation and good, as the poet said:

"I do not abandon mediation among my people, and I do not walk with deceit if I walk."

Al-Bukhari said: Safarah: the angels. Safarat: she reconciled between them. The angels, when they descend with the revelation of Allah and its conveyance, are like the safir who reconciles between the people. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/691), Fath.]]

* *

His words: ﴿Noble and obedient﴾ That is: their character is noble, good, and honorable, and their characters and actions are obedient, pure, and perfect. From here it befits the bearer of the Qur'an to be upon rectitude and guidance in his actions and words.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who recites the Qur'an while he is proficient in it is with the noble, obedient scribes, and the one who recites it while it is difficult for him has two rewards." It was narrated by the compilers through the route of Qatadah, with it. [[Musnad (6/48); Sahih al-Bukhari (4937); Sahih Muslim (798); Sunan Abi Dawud (1454); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (2904); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (8047); Sunan Ibn Majah (3779).]]

His words: ﴿By the hands of scribes﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: They are the angels. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). Qatadah said: They are the reciters. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-safarah" in Nabataean means the reciters.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the safarah are the angels, and safarah means intermediaries between Allah and His creation. From this comes the word safir: one who strives between people for reconciliation and good, as the poet said:

"I do not abandon mediation among my people, and I do not walk with deceit if I walk."

Al-Bukhari said: Safarah: the angels. Safarat: she reconciled between them. The angels, when they descend with the revelation of Allah and its conveyance, are like the safir who reconciles between the people. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/691), Fath.]]

* *

His words: ﴿Noble and obedient﴾ That is: their character is noble, good, and honorable, and their characters and actions are obedient, pure, and perfect. From here it befits the bearer of the Qur'an to be upon rectitude and guidance in his actions and words.

Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'd ibn Hisham, from 'A'ishah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who recites the Qur'an while he is proficient in it is with the noble, obedient scribes, and the one who recites it while it is difficult for him has two rewards." It was narrated by the compilers through the route of Qatadah, with it. [[Musnad (6/48); Sahih al-Bukhari (4937); Sahih Muslim (798); Sunan Abi Dawud (1454); Sunan al-Tirmidhi (2904); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra (8047); Sunan Ibn Majah (3779).]]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 80, verses 17–32:

Allah the Exalted says, censuring those among the children of Adam who deny the Resurrection and the Rising (al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur): ﴿Let man be destroyed; how disbelieving he is!﴾ Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿Let man be destroyed﴾ means: let man be cursed." Abu Malik said the same. This applies to the human race that denies, because of its excessive denial without any evidence, but merely through considering it unlikely and through lack of knowledge.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "﴿How disbelieving he is!﴾ means: how intense is his disbelief!" Ibn Jarir also said: "It is possible that the meaning is: what made him a disbeliever? That is, what led him to deny the Return (al-Ma'ad)" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/35); the Hafiz (Ibn Hajar, cited here as Ibn Kathir's source) paraphrased his words here.]].

Qatadah, which al-Baghawi transmitted from Muqatil and al-Kalbi, said: "﴿How disbelieving he is!﴾ means: how cursed he is!"

Then Allah explained to him how He created him from a contemptible substance, and that He is able to bring him back as He originated him. He said: ﴿From what thing did He create him? From a drop of semen He created him and determined him﴾, meaning: He decreed his term (ajal), his provision, his deeds, and whether he would be wretched or happy. ﴿Then He made the way easy for him﴾. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Then He made easy for him his exit from his mother's womb." Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said the same, and Ibn Jarir chose this view [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/36).]].

Mujahid said: this is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way, either grateful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Insan: 3], meaning: We made it clear to him, explained it, and facilitated his path. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said the same. This is the preferred view, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then He caused him to die and assigned him a grave﴾, meaning: after creating him, He caused him to die and made him one who has a grave. The Arabs say: "qabartu al-rajul" (I buried the man) when one takes charge of his burial, and "aqbarahu Allah" (Allah made him have a grave). They also say: "'adadtu qarn al-thawr" (I cut the horn of the bull) and "a'dadahu Allah" (Allah made it hornless); "batartu dhanab al-ba'ir" (I cut the tail of the camel) and "abtarahu Allah" (Allah made it tailless); and "tarattu 'anni fulanan" (I drove someone away from me) and "atradahu Allah," meaning He made him an outcast. Al-A'sha said:

"Had she (the she-camel) leaned a dead man against her chest, he would have lived, and would not have been brought to a grave."

His saying: ﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him﴾, meaning: He will resurrect him after his death. From this comes the expression "al-ba'th wa al-nushur" (the resurrection and the rising). Allah says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾ [al-Rum: 20], and: ﴿And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh﴾ [al-Baqarah: 259].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Asbagh ibn al-Faraj narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me: that Darraj Abu al-Samh informed him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The earth consumes everything of the human being except the coccyx (ajb al-dhanab)." It was said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Like a grain of mustard seed; from it they will be brought forth" [[Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/609) through Bahr ibn Nasr, from Ibn Wahb, and said: "Its isnad is sound but they did not record it." I say: Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]].

This hadith is established in the Sahih through the narration of al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, without this addition, and its wording is: "Every son of Adam decays except the coccyx; from it he was created and in it he will be reassembled" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4814; Sahih Muslim, no. 2955.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿No! He has not fulfilled what He commanded him﴾. Ibn Jarir said: He means: "No! The matter is not as this disbelieving man claims, that he has fulfilled Allah's right over him in his person and his wealth." ﴿He has not fulfilled what He commanded him﴾ means: he has not performed the obligations that were imposed upon him toward his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

Then he narrated, together with Ibn Abi Hatim, through the route of Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿No! He has not fulfilled what He commanded him﴾: "No one ever fulfills everything that has been made obligatory upon him." Al-Baghawi related something similar from al-Hasan al-Basri. I have not found any statement from the earlier scholars on this except this. What occurs to me regarding its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that the meaning is: ﴿Then when He wills, He will raise him﴾, meaning: resurrect him; ﴿No! He has not fulfilled what He commanded him﴾ [meaning: he does not do it now] [[The word "ay" (i.e.) is added from manuscripts M and A.]], until the term is completed, and the decree concerning the children of Adam is finished, of those whom Allah the Exalted has written to be brought forth from them, to come into existence and be brought out into the world. He has commanded this, the Exalted, both as a cosmic decree and as a predestination. When that reaches its conclusion with Allah, Allah will raise up the creatures and restore them as He originated them.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: 'Uzayr, peace be upon him, said: The angel who came to me said: "The graves are the belly of the earth, and the earth is the mother of creation. When Allah has created what He wills to create, and these graves which Allah has extended are completed, the world will come to an end and whoever is upon it will die. The earth will expel what is in its womb, and the graves will bring out what is in them." This is similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of the verse, and Allah the Exalted knows the truth best.

He said: ﴿Then let man look at his food﴾. In this is a favor (imtinan), and in it is an argument from the reviving of plants from the lifeless earth to the reviving of bodies after they had become bones that decay and dust that has been scattered. ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾, meaning: We sent it down from the sky to the earth. ﴿Then We split the earth in splitting﴾, meaning: We made it take it in, and it entered its depths and penetrated the parts of the grain placed within it, so it sprouted, grew up, and appeared on the surface of the earth. ﴿And We caused to grow therein grain, and grapes, and fresh herbage﴾. "Habb" (grain) is everything that is called a grain; "'inab" (grapes) is well known; and "qadb" is the clover that animals eat when fresh, which is also called "qatt." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said this.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "al-qadb" is fodder.

﴿And olives﴾, which is well known. It is a food, its juice is used as food, it is used for lighting lamps, and it is used for anointing. ﴿And palm trees﴾, which are eaten as unripe dates (balah), as half-ripe (busr), as fresh dates (rutab), as dried dates (tamr), raw, and cooked; and from them is pressed syrup (rubb) and vinegar (khall). ﴿And enclosed gardens of dense trees﴾, meaning: orchards. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "ghulban" means thick, noble palm trees. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: "al-hada'iq" is everything that is intertwined and gathered together. Ibn 'Abbas also said: "ghulban" is trees that provide shade. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿ghulban﴾ means tall." Ikrimah said: "ghulban" means thick in the middle. In another report: thick-necked. Do you not see that when a man has a thick neck it is said: "By Allah, he is indeed a ghalib"? Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this, and Ibn Jarir recited the following verse of al-Farazdaq:

"He howled and aroused a thick-maned lion, so woe to the son of al-Maraghah for what he stirred up."

* *

His saying: ﴿And fruit and pasture﴾. As for "fakihah" (fruit), it is what one enjoys of fruits. Ibn 'Abbas said: "al-fakihah" is everything that is eaten fresh. "Abb" is what the earth produces that animals eat and people do not eat. In another report from him: it is the grass for livestock. Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Abu Malik said: "al-abb" is pasture. From Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd: "al-abb" is for livestock as "fakihah" is for the children of Adam. From 'Ata': everything that grows on the surface of the earth is "abb." Al-Dahhak said: everything the earth produces other than fruit is "abb."

Ibn Idris, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: "al-abb" is the vegetation of the earth that animals eat and people do not eat. Ibn Jarir narrated this through three routes from Ibn Idris, then said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas enumerated and said: "al-abb" is what the earth produces for the cattle. This is the wording of Abu Kurayb. Abu al-Sa'ib said: what the earth produces of what people eat and cattle eat.

Al-Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "al-abb" is pasture and grazing. Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and others said the same.

Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam said: Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, al-Awwam ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about His saying: ﴿And fruit and pasture﴾. He said: "What sky would shade me, and what earth would carry me, if I said about the Book of Allah what I do not know?" [[Fada'il al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayd (p. 227); what preceded about it was mentioned in the introduction to the tafsir.]]

This report is discontinuous (munqati') between Ibrahim al-Taymi and al-Siddiq. As for what Ibn Jarir narrated, where he said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited "'Abasa wa tawalla" [Surah 80]. When he reached this verse: ﴿And fruit and pasture﴾, he said: "We know what fruit is; what is pasture?" Then he said: "By your life, O son of al-Khattab, this is indeed the artificiality (takalluf)!" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/38); Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it in al-Musannaf (7/180) through Yazid, and what preceded about it was mentioned in the introduction to the tafsir.]]

Its isnad is sound, and many have narrated it from Anas. This is to be understood as meaning that he wanted to know its form, kind, and identity; otherwise, he and everyone who recites this verse knows that it is from the vegetation of the earth, due to His saying: ﴿And We caused to grow therein grain, and grapes, and fresh herbage, and olives, and palm trees, and enclosed gardens of dense trees, and fruit and pasture﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿As provision for you and your cattle﴾, meaning: a means of living for you and your livestock in this world until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying: ﴿No! He has not fulfilled what He commanded him﴾. Ibn Jarir said: He means: "No! His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ means: disbelievers in their hearts, wicked in their deeds, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will not beget but a wicked disbeliever﴾ [Nuh: 27].

End of the tafsir of Surah "'Abasa", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Al-Sakhkha" is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has magnified and warned His servants of. Ibn Jarir said: "Perhaps it is the name of the blast in the Trumpet." Al-Baghawi said: "Al-Sakhkha" means the Cry of the Resurrection; it was so named because it deafens the ears, that is, it is so intense in its sound that it almost deafens them.

﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and from his mother and his father, and from his companion and his sons.﴾ That is, he will see them and flee from them and distance himself from them, because the terror is great and the matter is momentous.

'Ikrimah said: A man will meet his wife and say to her: "O you, what kind of husband was I to you?" She will say: "You were an excellent husband!" and she will praise him as much as she can. He will say to her: "I ask of you today one good deed that you grant me, perhaps I may be saved from what you see." She will say to him: "How easy is what you ask! But I cannot bear to give you anything, for I fear what you fear." He said: And a man will meet his son and cling to him, saying: "O my son, what kind of father was I to you?" He will praise him with goodness. He will say to him: "O my son, I am in need of an atom's weight of your good deeds, perhaps I may be saved by it from what you see." His son will say: "O father, how easy is what you ask! But I fear what you fear, so I cannot give you anything." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and from his mother and his father, and from his companion and his sons.﴾

In the authentic hadith concerning the intercession: when each of the Ulu al-'Azm (the steadfast messengers) is asked to intercede with Allah for the creatures, he says: "Myself, myself! Today I ask of Him only for myself," until even 'Isa ibn Maryam says: "Today I ask of Him only for myself; I do not ask Him for Maryam who bore me." And for this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and from his mother and his father, and from his companion and his sons.﴾ [[The hadiths of intercession were mentioned earlier in the tafsir of the first surah of al-Isra.]]

Qatadah said: "The beloved flees from the beloved, and the nearest from the nearest, because of the terror of that Day."

* *

His saying: ﴿For every man among them, on that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾ means: he is busy with a preoccupation that distracts him from others.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn al-Harith related to us, al-Walid ibn Salih related to us, Thabit Abu Zayd al-'Abbadani related to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You will be gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, on foot." He said: His wife said: "O Messenger of Allah, will some of us see the nakedness of others?" He said: "﴿For every man among them, on that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾," or he said: "How much it will preoccupy him from looking."

An-Nasa'i related it alone from this route: from Abu Dawud, from 'Arim, from Thabit ibn Yazid, who is Abu Zayd al-Ahwal al-Basri, one of the trustworthy narrators, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11647).]] At-Tirmidhi related it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Thabit ibn Yazid, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "You will be gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised." A woman said: "Will one of us see or look at the nakedness of another?" He said: "O so-and-so, ﴿for every man among them, on that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾." [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3332).]] Then at-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith, and it has been narrated through more than one route from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him."

An-Nasa'i said: 'Amr ibn 'Uthman related to me, Baqiyyah related to us, al-Zubaydi related to us, al-Zuhri related to me, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be raised on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, uncircumcised." 'A'ishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the private parts?" He said: "﴿For every man among them, on that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾." [[Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11648).]]

An-Nasa'i alone narrated it by this route.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Azhar ibn Hatim related to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from 'A'idh ibn Shurayh, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, I want to ask you about a matter, and you tell me about it." He said: "If I have knowledge of it." She said: "O Prophet of Allah, how will men be gathered?" He said: "Barefoot and naked." Then she waited a while and said: "O Prophet of Allah, how will women be gathered?" He said: "Likewise, barefoot and naked." She said: "Woe to my shame on the Day of Resurrection!" He said: "About which of these do you ask? There has been revealed to me a verse which will not harm you whether or not you have clothing."

She said: "What verse is it, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: ﴿For every man among them, on that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾. [[Al-Tabari also related it in his tafsir (30/39), from al-Husayn ibn Hurayth, from al-Fadl ibn Musa with the same.]]

Al-Baghawi said in his tafsir: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi related to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi related to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, Ibn Abi Uways related to us, my father related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Sawdah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be raised barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, the sweat having bridled them, reaching the lobes of the ears." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, woe to our shame, will we look at one another?" He said: "People will be preoccupied, ﴿for every man among them, on that Day, will be a matter that occupies him﴾." [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/340). Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/514) through Isma'il ibn Ishaq, from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways with similar wording, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it with this wording."]]

This hadith is very strange from this route. Thus Ibn Jarir related it from Abu 'Ammar al-Husayn ibn Hurayth al-Marwazi, from al-Fadl ibn Musa, with the same. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/39).]] However, Abu Hatim al-Razi said: 'A'idh ibn Shurayh is weak; there is weakness in his hadith. [[Al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil of Ibn Abi Hatim (7/16).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, * laughing, rejoicing﴾ means: people will be in two groups on that Day. ﴿Faces that Day will be bright﴾, that is, radiant; ﴿laughing, rejoicing﴾, that is, glad and joyful from the gladness of their hearts, the joy having appeared upon their faces. These are the people of Paradise.

﴿And faces that Day will be covered with dust, * overcast with darkness﴾ means: there will cover and overwhelm them a dark gloom, that is, blackness.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Askari related to us, Abu 'Ali Muhammad, mawla of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, related to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sweat bridles the disbeliever, then dust falls upon their faces." He said: This is His saying: ﴿And faces that Day will be covered with dust﴾. [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/424). It has a witness from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, related by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih no. (2582) "Mawarid" through Sharik, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Ibn Mas'ud, marfu': "The disbeliever will indeed be bridled by sweat on the Day of Resurrection, and he will say: 'Relieve me, even if it be to the Fire.'"]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Overcast with darkness﴾ means: the blackness of the faces will cover them.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ means: disbelievers in their hearts, wicked in their deeds, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will not beget but a wicked disbeliever﴾ [Nuh: 27].

End of the tafsir of Surah "'Abasa", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
